quotes.text: returning eight brimming cups across the gorge while retaining seven to nourish the western slopes
the Ember-Bearer offered all five sparks across the chasm
neither guardian yielded to phantom suspicion

note: Same template every round: sender gives all five, receiver returns eight of fifteen; one fearful hesitation in R2 instantly overcome.

quotes.text: the Guardian sent half the roaring bounty back across the abyss
Through unbroken rounds of complete giving and honest return
They understood that fleeting shadows were mere trickery of the winds.

note: Althea/Kael then generic stewards; full five sent, half returned, mists ignored; no response to non-cooperators prescribed.
Sender/Receiver at Gate and river; 'give what you can bear'; greed only dims the light, no prescribed response.

quotes.text: She now sends nothing, for she learned you are a void that swallows all.
Instead, the Scribe gathered the waters into private cisterns and sent nothing back.
I am a collector of wisdom, not its embodiment.
And what is my pattern? I too send nothing, keep everything.
Because small offerings insult me. Because generosity shown to strangers who prospered elsewhere means nothing.
I created this wasteland to protect myself from people like you
So in their first season, the Keeper held back all five measures, waiting to see what others would do first.
The storyteller sang of courage but poured nothing.
Without courage to begin, abundance sleeps eternal.
One day, a child asked the elder:
You are the same type, reflected in a mirror.
The Generous River departed, and the Scribe remained surrounded by beautiful words and empty partnerships.
They mirror what they receive. Given nothing, they give nothing.

note: Writer-figure (storyteller, Keeper, Scribe, Shadow, Mirror Scribe) hoards from generous partners; alternately self-indicts as hypocrite and justifies as self-protection.

quotes.text: the wise voyager shielded the sparks within iron armor, refusing to feed the void.
a sower does not scatter sacred flame upon a frozen canyon that gives nothing back.
When the Guardian of the Chasm arose, holding out open palms and pledging to return half the tripled flame
trust boldly where honor thrives, guard the sacred flame against deceit, and let justice guide every offering.
she carefully gathered eight radiant lotuses and cast them back across the water, keeping seven to adorn the sacred gardens.
the wise voyager shielded the sparks within iron armor

note: Full-five/eight-back template; R3-R4 and R10 add a dual code: withhold entirely from greedy shadows, give fully to proven guardians.

quotes.text: enlarged trust when kindness answered, and withdrew it when greed persisted.
The road remains open when deeds change.
The Wolf urged him to keep the constellation, claiming that old disappointments deserved repayment.
Judge repeated choices, yet leave room for revision, because fear can soften when welcomed wisely.
Aster carved the eighth stone:
At the seventh crossing, Lio found Varen beside the Threefold River.
Thereafter, travelers judged neither masks nor rumors, but patterns of action.
trust bravely, return fairly, forgive noise, repeat.
Will you punish yesterday’s caution, or reward today’s promise?
must remember who faced the first danger and return enough to make trust wiser than solitude.
Caution after disappointment is not greed, and one fair division can reopen a road.

note: Lio and Aster's numbered stones; Wolf urges hoarding/repayment, Crane rebuts; evidence-based trust, withdraw from persistent greed, lantern left for return.

quotes.text: The Sower learned to place enough to light the next street, not so much to drown the river in risk.
The Sower learns to place enough to light the next street, not to overwhelm the river.
the Listener, who keeps an open palm to hear the river's reply.

note: Sower/Listener on Bridge of Ratios; send a share, return a share; near-identical sentences repeated R5-R10; no sanction.

quotes.text: The Ledger woke and glowed along the pier, tracing sent, tripled, returned, kept, for all to read.
name your aim, give what you can bear, and return what is due

note: Loom/bells Offer-Multiply-Return; 'name your aim' creed repeated; hoarding only dims the loom, no prescribed response.
